quarterly_data.signal: DATA-CENTER ORDER BOOK SIZED: CEO Lorenzo Simonelli said 'since 2025, IET has secured $4.2 billion of data center-related orders, including approximately $3.2 billion in the first half of 2026 alone', and separately that 'Chart Industries has booked approximately $600 million of data center orders over the past two years'. The combined offer is pitched as a facility-level solution rather than individual products as power density rises: Baker Hughes supplies on-site power generation, power conversion and microgrid control for reliability and uptime, while Chart adds cooling infrastructure, carbon capture, water treatment and recycling, and LNG and hydrogen storage and backup fuel systems. He said commercial engagement between the two teams is already underway, 'particularly around data center infrastructure and broader gas infrastructure opportunities'.
quarterly_data.figure: IET data center-related orders $4.2 billion since 2025, including approximately $3.2 billion in the first half of 2026; Chart approximately $600 million of data center orders over the past two years

quarterly_data.signal: THE IET BACKLOG BEHIND IT: first-half 2026 IET orders of '$12 billion', a record IET RPO of 'more than $37 billion at the end of the second quarter' - this is the IET segment figure, not the company-wide total - and a reaffirmed 'more than $45 billion of IET orders through the Horizon Two period'. IET delivered record EBITDA margins of 18.5% in 2025 and Simonelli said he expects margins 'to exceed 20% in 2026', with a clear path to 20% adjusted EBITDA margins for Baker Hughes by 2028 excluding Chart. Approximately 60% of company revenue now comes from infrastructure and industrial markets, and OFSE margins are up more than 600 basis points since 2017.
quarterly_data.figure: IET EBITDA margin record 18.5% in 2025, expected to exceed 20% in 2026; clear path to 20% company adjusted EBITDA margin by 2028 excluding Chart; ~60% of revenue from infrastructure and industrial (reaffirmed from the Q2 call: H1 IET orders $12 billion, IET RPO more than $37 billion, more than $45 billion of IET orders through Horizon Two)

quarterly_data.signal: CHART INTEGRATION MECHANICS AND THE BACKLOG RESTATEMENT: after a preliminary contract-level review and the application of Baker Hughes' own backlog definitions, Chart's reported backlog drops to 'approximately $3.6 billion at the end of the third quarter'. Simonelli insisted this is 'a methodology change to align with the integration that we are conducting... not an end market view', with Chart book-to-bill still above one in the second half. On synergies, 'we have already executed $35 million of actions to date' toward 'approximately $325 million of annualized cost synergies by year 3', roughly three-quarters of it captured inside the Chart segment - part of '500 to 600 basis points of margin expansion over the next two years' that takes Chart EBITDA margin from about 17% in the second half of 2026 to '22%-23% by the second half of 2028'. Near-term Chart margin is held back by the timing of LNG equipment volumes, soft hydrogen demand and several first-of-a-kind projects with lower margin profiles; he sees improving visibility toward an LNG order recovery moving into 2027. Second-half Chart EBITDA is weighted about 40% third quarter and 60% fourth quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: $35 million of synergy actions already executed (approximately three-quarters of the $325 million to be captured inside the Chart segment); Chart EBITDA margin from approximately 17% in the second half of 2026 to 22%-23% by the second half of 2028, 500 to 600 basis points of expansion; second-half Chart EBITDA split about 40% Q3 / 60% Q4 (Chart backlog restatement to ~$3.6 billion and the $325 million target were already disclosed)

quarterly_data.signal: MARKET SIZE RE-FRAMED WITH CHART: 'Combined with Chart, we now compete across an addressable market of more than $400 billion.' Within that, exposure to the high-growth end markets - gas infrastructure, geothermal, data centers, carbon capture, space, mining and industrial gases - rises 'nearly 60%, from approximately $36 billion today to roughly $57 billion by 2030'. Simonelli also cited 'a growing enterprise solutions pipeline of $10 billion'. This is a wider cut than the power systems TAM Baker Hughes has framed before, because it spans the full combined portfolio.
quarterly_data.figure: combined addressable market more than $400 billion; high-growth end-market exposure up nearly 60%, from approximately $36 billion today to roughly $57 billion by 2030; enterprise solutions pipeline of $10 billion
